capture.final_message:
Treat all four universally quantified statements as independently true; then each `Iff` follows by sending either hypothesis to the unconditional proof of the opposite side.

The common mechanism is to unfold membership in the relevant sets:

- `a ∈ fixedPoints M α` means `∀ m, m • a = a`, exactly membership in `⋂ m, fixedBy m`.
- `Quotient.orbit x` is the fiber/equivalence class represented by `x`. The right inverse `φ` ensures `φ x` represents `x`, and for a group action the orbit relation class of `φ x` is precisely `orbit G (φ x)`.
- Every quotient orbit is nonempty: use quotient induction on `x`; a representative belongs to its own class.
- A monoid orbit is closed under the action. If `y = n • a`, then
  `m • y = (m * n) • a`, so `m • y` remains in `orbit M a`.

Organize the result by splitting the outer `And`, constructing both `Iff`s, and proving their directions using these unconditional lemmas. The group assumption is essential only when identifying an orbit-relation equivalence class with an ordinary orbit; monoid structure already suffices for orbit closure.
